title: Change window negotiation and summary ledger PRD
content:
Purpose:

This PRD proposes a lightweight protocol and product workflow for scheduled network/ops changes in customer-managed/private deployments: a Change Window Negotiation (CWN) flow + a Compact Change Summary Ledger (CCSL) emitted as the primary audit artifact. The goal is to reduce friction for customer operators who need predictable maintenance windows while keeping Redwood and customers aligned on what happened, when, and why — without shipping verbose full-packet telemetry or heavy forensic bundles by default.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Customers running Private deployments require predictable maintenance windows for infra/network changes (e.g., firewall rule updates, edge connector upgrades, operator configuration) to satisfy their own compliance and change management processes.
- Current options: ad-hoc emails, manual tickets, or the full attestation/evidence bundles we use internally. Those are either error-prone or heavy and slow to generate and review.
- Product team needs a standard surface: 1) to accept/acknowledge proposed windows, 2) to coordinate short pre-approval checks (capacity, model compatibility), and 3) to emit a compact, tamper-evident summary that customers can store in their compliance systems.

Success metrics (6–12 weeks):
- Reduce back-and-forth with customer ops teams during scheduled maintenance by 60% compared to baseline support tickets.
- Produce a Compact Change Summary for 90% of scheduled windows (lightweight mode), reserving full forensic bundles for incident/forensic requests.
- Achieve <5% failure rate in the negotiation handshake (timeouts, mismatched windows) in pilot accounts.

User personas:
- Customer Network Admin (primary): needs to announce planned changes and receive an agreed window and minimal proof of execution.
- Customer Security Compliance Officer: consumes ledger entries as proof-of-change; needs minimal fields and stable hashes for retention.
- Redwood Operator: validates compatibility checks, schedules internal maintenance on Dedicated resources or routes customer-scheduled changes to on-prem agents.

High-level flow:
1) Customer proposes a Change Window via Console/API indicating: target scope (tenant, site, agent id), start/end UTC window, change type (config/network/upgrade), and optional brief rationale.
2) Redwood validates: automated policy checks (compatibility, model-bound SLOs, active rollouts), then responds with: accept / propose adjusted window / reject.
3) If accepted, both sides persist a `Negotiated Window` record with an increasing sequence id and per-record compact digest (SHA256).
4) During the window, Redwood (or customer agent) emits one or more Compact Change Summaries to a ledger: a succinct single-line entry per atomic action plus a final window-close summary that contains the digest chain root.
5) Customer and Redwood retain the CCSL entry (and ability to request a forensic bundle if needed).

Product components:
- Console + API: "Schedule change" modal and REST endpoint (POST /v1/private/change-windows).
- Negotiation service: policy checks, time-zone normalizations, conflict detection, sequencing, and digesting.
- Ledger service (compact): append-only compact records per window, exportable as newline-delimited JSONL compressed, with optional signed envelope.
- Agent/sidecar hooks: for on-prem customers we allow a small agent to coordinate the local change and push CCSL fragments back to the ledger over the private control plane.

Compact Change Summary Ledger (CCSL) schema (lightweight):
- window_id: string (opaque id)
- seq: int (monotonic entry number for the window)
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp
- actor: short string (redwood/operator/customer-agent)
- action: short verb (e.g., rule-add, rule-remove, ip-block, connector-upgrade)
- scope: short descriptor (tenant:abc, site:west, agent:agent-123)
- result: OK | WARN | FAIL
- brief: single-line freeform reason
- prev_digest: hex (SHA256 of previous entry in window)
- digest: hex (SHA256 of canonicalized entry)

Note: CCSL is intentionally minimal to allow fast storage in customer SIEMs and to keep retention cheap. The ledger file for a window is expected to be <50KB in typical operations. For forensic needs we will provide a full evidence bundle (verbose logs, packet captures, attestation tokens) on request and gated by an audit process.

Approval gates and policy checks (behavior):
- On propose: run quick checks that are O(1) or O(number of models pinned to tenant):
  - Does the window overlap high-SLA model rollouts? If yes, respond with a suggested adjusted window (algorithm: shift by earliest non-conflicting 1–6 hour slot within 72h).
  - Does the change scope include dedicated hardware that would drop throughput below reserved capacity? If so, include a mitigation note.
  - Validate that the requesting principal has the right IAM role (customer operator or delegated admin).
- Human review escalation: if a check flags high-risk (multi-tenant cross-dependencies), escalate to a Redwood on-call with templated context.

UX considerations (Console):
- Minimal mode (default): Customer selects scope, start/end, and reason; shows likely conflicts inline and auto-suggested alternatives. Agreement is one click.
- Pro mode (enterprise): allows attaching a short runbook (text) and selecting whether CCSL entries are signed with customer-managed keys (KMIP/KMS HSM integration).
- Notifications: webhook + email + console activity feed.

Security and tamper-evidence:
- Ledger digests are chained per-window. Ledger files are signed server-side with Redwood rotating keys; customers can opt-in to have the final root signed by their KMS key (customer-managed signing).
- Minimum retention: Redwood retains CCSL files per contract (default 90 days). Customers can request longer retention or export for their SIEM.

Failure modes / open scenarios:
- Missed agent heartbeats during an agreed window: behavior is to mark affected actions with result=WARN and include agent heartbeat snapshot.
- Divergent views: if customer agent claims an action and Redwood has no matching CC entry, we provide reconciliation tooling to diff both sides and produce an escrowed forensic request.
- Time sync drift: require NTP-validated timestamps; if >5s drift detected, include clock-drift note in the ledger entry and escalate per policy.

Backward compatibility and pilot plan:
- Phase 0 (pilot): implement API + Console scheduling + compact ledger (no KMS signing). Pilot with 3 customers (one Dedicated, two Private VPCs).
- Phase 1: agent-side integration for on-prem push of CCSL fragments and optional customer signing.
- Phase 2: add forensic bundle on-demand tooling and retention controls in Console.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How frequently do customers want full forensic bundles vs. compact summaries? (We expect heavy savings if <10% ask for full bundles.)
- Policy complexity: do we encode more domain-specific checks (e.g., model families that cannot be interrupted) or keep the negotiation engine generic?
- Legal: does a compact ledger entry meet audit requirements in key regulated customers? We should validate with legal and 2 pilot customers.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- API owner: Ethan to draft API schema and OpenAPI contract (PD-1123).
- Engineer experiment: Priya to prototype a tiny ledger writer service + console modal mock.
- SRE/Infra: Liam to estimate storage/retention cost per 10k windows/month and agent env packaging.
- Schedule pilot outreach: reach out to two current Private customers for interest in a November pilot.

Appendix: example CCSL entry (canonicalized single-line JSON)
{"window_id":"wnd-20241105-az1-7","seq":1,"ts":"2024-11-05T01:00:12Z","actor":"agent-182","action":"rule-add","scope":"tenant:acme-corp;site:az1","result":"OK","brief":"added egress deny 10.0.0.0/8 for test-batch","prev_digest":"000000...","digest":"afe3c4..."}

Note: this is a draft intended for team review. Comments welcome; I'll convert to a more formal PRD after pilot validation.
